card.name: Have or has after adverse-event subjects
card.fires_on: The auxiliary 'have' or 'has' (sometimes 'also') right after a plural or abstract subject like symptoms, reactions or events, in adverse-effect text. It comes just before a past participle such as 'been reported' or 'occurred'.

modes.label: Symptoms have
modes.description: 'have' directly after a symptom or reaction noun, before a participle like been or resolved.
modes.example: Symptoms<< have>> resolved after discontinuation of XOSPATA

modes.label: Singular has
modes.description: 'has' after a singular event or outcome noun, before been or not always occurred.
modes.example: Full recovery from these adverse reactions<< has>> not always occurred with cessation of therapy with

modes.label: Have also
modes.description: 'also' placed between have and been in a reporting sentence.
modes.example: However, cardiac events have<< also>> been reported in adults and children without underlying

card.writes: It pushes toward words meaning 'so far' or 'to date' (bisher, 迄今为止, これまで), as in 'has been reported to date'.
card.plain: It fires on 'have' or 'has' after a side-effect subject, where the text is about to say what has been reported so far.
